clue.text: Tie up credit frequently for ceramics factory

parts.note: to moor a boat is to tie it up

explanation.surface: A bank instruction to lock in credit regularly for a pottery works.
explanation.walkthrough: Moorcroft is a well-known pottery company in Stoke-on-Trent, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Moorcroft is the name of a Staffordshire pottery manufacturer, an example of a ceramics factory.

clue.text: Ireland releases information after hoarder makes plea for mercy

indicators.note: after means following, so the country's remains come behind the miser
releasing something lets it go, so that letter leaves the country's name

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name of Ireland
I is the abbreviation for information

explanation.surface: Ireland gives up data after a stingy person pleads for leniency.
explanation.walkthrough: Eire is Ireland's name in Irish, and 'releases' means the country lets one letter go before the remains follow the hoarder.
explanation.definitionFit: Miserere is the Latin opening of Psalm 51, 'Have mercy', and names any such appeal for pity.

clue.text: Character has ring that's enormous

explanation.surface: A person wears a gigantic ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the last letter of the Greek alphabet, and a letter is a character.

clue.text: Funny film about case you've kept up in the air?

definitions.meaning: setter's reading: a comic film in the British series famous for innuendo, imagined as being about a suitcase

definitions.text: you've kept up in the air
definitions.meaning: surface reading: a bag held aloft, but really the bag you keep with you in the aircraft cabin

explanation.surface: A comedy movie about a bag someone held above their head.
explanation.walkthrough: The Carry On films were a long-running series of British comedies, so a Carry On about baggage would be one.
explanation.definitionFit: Hand baggage taken aboard a plane and stowed in the cabin is with you while you fly.

clue.text: She provides an endless series of games

parts.note: taken as the article, part of the description

indicators.note: something endless has no end, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: an Olympiad is a staging of the Olympic Games

explanation.surface: A woman who supplies a never-ending run of contests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'She' stands for a woman's name; Olympia is one.
explanation.definitionFit: Olympia is a female first name, so it can stand for a woman referred to as she.

clue.text: Everything in note demanding silence is somewhat implausible

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the first piece goes within the musical syllable

parts.note: ti is a note of the sol-fa scale
sh is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: A complete musical note that calls for quiet seems rather far-fetched.
explanation.walkthrough: A tall story is an unlikely one, so tallish means a bit hard to believe.
explanation.definitionFit: Tall can mean exaggerated or unlikely, as in a tall tale, so tallish means rather far-fetched.

clue.text: Brought up to talk about money in an informal way

indicators.note: talking about something means saying it out loud, so we want a word that sounds like the slang term

explanation.surface: Someone raised to discuss cash casually.
explanation.definitionFit: Bred is the past participle of breed, meaning raised or reared, just as a child is brought up.

clue.text: It's rare seeing her here juggling with two clubs

indicators.note: juggling things tosses them about, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs in cards, twice

explanation.surface: An unusual sight: a woman here juggling a pair of clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Recherché, from French, means choice or exquisite, hence uncommon and hard to find.

clue.text: Amount of drugs given by guru after party

indicators.note: after means following, so the wise person comes behind the celebration

parts.note: a sage is a wise teacher

explanation.surface: A spiritual teacher hands out narcotics following a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A dosage is the measured quantity of a medicine to be taken.

clue.text: Helpless gent is tossing during it — advise 17 perhaps

indicators.note: tossing means throwing about, so the letters land in a different order

explanation.surface: A powerless man is tossing and turning in bed, so suggest he count sheep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tossing' does double duty in the surface, describing the restless sleeper; 17 refers to the across answer, the classic insomnia cure.
explanation.definitionFit: A night without sleep is the time when you might be told to try counting sheep.

clue.text: Dirty sort of business a Republican goes after

indicators.note: going after means following, so the later pieces come behind the first

parts.note: small or medium-sized enterprise, a category of business

explanation.surface: A grubby kind of enterprise is being pursued by a Republican politician.
explanation.walkthrough: SME (small and medium-sized enterprise) is a common business abbreviation in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: To smear is to soil or make something grubby, a verb sense of dirty.

clue.text: Skye local managed to provide security apparatus

indicators.note: managed suggests letters being handled and organised into a new order

explanation.surface: A resident of the Scottish island of Skye organised the installation of security.
explanation.walkthrough: Skye is an island in the Scottish Hebrides; a Yale lock is a common pin-tumbler door lock.
explanation.definitionFit: Yale locks are door fastenings, devices that keep a building secure.

clue.text: Prepared ahead to deliver scam

parts.note: as in two goals up, meaning in front

explanation.surface: Someone is all set in advance to pull off a con.
explanation.walkthrough: To ready up is Australian slang for rigging or swindling, chiefly in fixing a race or deal.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australian slang, to ready up is to fix or rig something dishonestly, which is a verb meaning to swindle.

clue.text: Murder composer that's challenging, cold and dangerous

definitions.note: adjectives describing the answer rather than a noun naming it

explanation.surface: A violent, difficult piece of music by a modern composer.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is descriptive: the thing that is challenging to ships, cold and dangerous.
explanation.definitionFit: A floating mass of ice is frigid and a notorious hazard to shipping, as the Titanic found.

clue.text: Religious type initially essential to churches

parts.words: Religious type initially essential to churches
parts.note: surface reading: a believer who is fundamental to churchgoing from the start; setter's reading: the answer's initials, R and C, sit at the very centre of the word churches

explanation.surface: A devout person was from the beginning vital to the church.
explanation.walkthrough: Look at the middle of 'churches': its core letters are R and C, the usual abbreviation for this denomination.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Church headed by the Pope is a particular kind of religious believer.

clue.text: Small and flexible doesn't quite describe an IT company

explanation.surface: Describing a computing giant as tiny and pliable would be inaccurate.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that the company's name literally reads small and soft, though it is neither.
explanation.definitionFit: Microsoft is the American technology corporation behind Windows and Office.

clue.text: Start betting with something that's easy to understand

parts.note: a bookmaker's book records the bets taken

explanation.surface: Begin wagering on something simple.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone described as an open book is transparent, easily read and understood.

clue.text: Agricultural stocktaking can put you out

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a farmer tallying the flock
second meaning: the traditional remedy for insomnia

explanation.walkthrough: 'Put you out' here means send you to sleep, not inconvenience you.
explanation.definitionFit: Tallying livestock on a farm is literal inventory, and the same mental exercise is the folk method for dropping off to sleep.

clue.text: Adviser using time in the US to break bank

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: a bank of seats is a tier
Pacific Standard Time, a US time zone

explanation.surface: A financial consultant uses American time to break a bank.
explanation.definitionFit: A tipster gives racing or investment tips, which is to say advice.

clue.text: Travelling around new domain with Charles

indicators.note: something new is remade, so the letters take a fresh arrangement

parts.note: C is an abbreviation for Charles

explanation.surface: Touring a fresh territory alongside a man called Charles.
explanation.definitionFit: Nomadic people have no fixed home and move from place to place.

clue.text: State authorises subversive regiment to be gutted

indicators.note: gutting removes the insides, so only the outside letters of each word survive

explanation.surface: A government sanctions the dismantling of a rebellious army unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a country, but it is the verb, and all three of the next words are gutted.
explanation.definitionFit: To assert something is to declare it firmly, which is to state it.

clue.text: Fool takes on leading German — it shouldn't last long

indicators.note: to take something on is to take it in, so the fool's letters wrap around the rest

parts.note: a sap is a gullible person

explanation.surface: A foolish person challenges a top German figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A temporary measure is meant only to fill a gap until something permanent arrives.

clue.text: Satellite includes operating pole that shows seasonal weather

indicators.note: something that includes another thing holds it inside

parts.note: the Moon is Earth's natural satellite
a machine that is on is operating

explanation.surface: A moon with a working pole reveals what the weather is doing.
explanation.definitionFit: The rainy season of South Asia is a wind and rain pattern that returns each year.

clue.text: Some boredom a hazard in US city

indicators.note: some means a part of, so the letters lie inside the words that follow

parts.note: found running across the end of the first word and into the next two

explanation.surface: A little tedium is a risk in an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: Omaha is the largest city in the state of Nebraska.

clue.text: Do a gentle twist when stretched

indicators.note: to twist something is to bend it out of its original shape

explanation.surface: An exercise instruction: perform a soft twist while doing a stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: Something elongated has been made longer, just as a thing stretched out is lengthened.

clue.text: Gouda in box occasionally includes fertiliser

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter is kept

parts.note: first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth letters

explanation.surface: A boxed cheese now and then comes packed with manure.
explanation.definitionFit: Guano is seabird or bat droppings, collected and spread on fields to enrich the soil.

clue.text: Betting group starts targeting operations that eventually …

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters, so we take one from each

parts.note: the first letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: A gambling syndicate begins aiming at business ventures that will eventually lead on to the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs this clue into the next one in surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tote is the pool-betting organisation on British racecourses, where stakes are pooled and shared among winners.

clue.text: … locate stand for Spooner where bets are placed

indicators.note: Spooner was famous for swapping the opening sounds of words, so the starts of the two words trade places

parts.note: to trace is to track down or find
a rack is a stand for holding things
the two words just found, with their opening sounds swapped as Spooner would

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, find a stand at the place where wagers are laid.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the opening sounds of TRACE RACK: the TR and R trade places to give RACE TRACK.
explanation.definitionFit: A racecourse is a venue where punters stake money on the outcome of races.
